newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Report on S.Africa Saldanha oil storage due in May.
newsitem.headline: Report on S.Africa Saldanha oil storage due in May.

text.p: A draft report on the environmental impact of commercialising the Strategic Fuel Fund's Saldanha oil storage terminal should be released at the end of May, Central Energy Fund acting general manager Howard Roberts aid on Thursday.
"The report will be issued to the interested and affected parties for their review and comment as well as to the independent review panel of experts on the topic," he told Reuters.
Their comments would be included in a final report to be issued later.

The study is being undertaken by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research and was started at the beginning of 1996 after SFF had announced that Iran was interested in storing some of its surplus oil stocks at the 45 million barrel facility.
There was widespread public concern that the increased tanker traffic would have adverse environmental effects on the sensitive wetlands around Saldanha.
"Arrangements to store oil at Saldanha for the Iranians are on hold pending the final outcome of the environmental impact study," Roberts said.
Roberts said progress in reducing South Africa's oil stockpile built up under apartheid era sanctions was ongoing.
"No stock reduction is taking place at Saldanha, but SFF still has excess stock at Ogies which is being worked down by sales to Natref (owned by Sasol and Total)," he said.
"Stocks at Ogies should reach the desired levels within the next few months."
The government decided last year to reduce the stockpile to 36 million barrels from 48 million barrels.
